en.title: Meet the language
en.intro:
A program starts as instructions you can read, predict and change. In this module, you will make a small desk sign, put two printed lines in order, distinguish message text from source punctuation, and greet a name received through input. Each lesson begins with a concrete program so you can try an idea before learning every symbol around it. Choose Java, Python, JavaScript or TypeScript; switching tracks keeps separate work, and the underlying idea stays the same.

Begin with a guess, then run the example and compare what happened. Investigate one statement at a time before making the requested change. The exercise ladder offers supplied examples, smaller completions and one independent welcome-slip program. You can revisit a rung whenever that support is useful. Hints are optional and reveal one next step at a time.

Your final checkpoint asks you to retrieve these ideas without the lesson in front of you. It is a chance to find what needs another look, not a countdown or an integrity test. Progress and explanations stay on this device. Java browser runs require your configured endpoint; local JDK instructions remain available when browser execution is unavailable.
en.recallPrompt: Before opening the first lesson, what is the difference between an instruction you write and the output you expect it to produce?
